# Ohmega Monster

> An intelligence engine: researched, graded reporting on world events. Every published article
> has a machine-readable twin listing its claims, how sure we are of each, and what each rests on.

Prefer the data files below to scraping article pages: they carry the grades and sources the prose
compresses away.

## Data

- [Article index](https://www.ohmega.monster/data/index.json): every article with a data twin, newest first.
- Article twin: `https://www.ohmega.monster/data/articles/<slug>.json`, where `<slug>` is the last path
  segment of the article URL. Each article page also links to its twin (`rel="alternate"`,
  `type="application/json"`).

Twin schema `ohmega.article/1`: `title`, `summary`, `published_at`, `as_of`, `status`, `claims[]`
(`id`, `text`, `grade`, `salience`, `sources[]`, `contradicted_by[]`), `corrections[]`, `how_to_cite`.

## Intelligence

- [Pulses](https://www.ohmega.monster/data/pulses.json) (`ohmega.pulses/1`): Ohmega's persistent
  readings of world dimensions, each a 0-100 position on one question (0 = the calm end, 100 = the
  extreme end, both described in `low_end` / `high_end`), with `band`, `confidence`, `history[]`
  and the latest reasoning. Early readings, still calibrating.
- [Intelligence index](https://www.ohmega.monster/data/intel.json) (`ohmega.intel.index/1`): the
  daily reports (`/geopolitics/<date>`), the deep briefs (`/intel/briefs/<slug>`), the theaters now
  being watched with their heat, and the public forecast scorecard.
- Daily reports and briefs separate what our research established (`researched`) from what other
  outlets reported (`reported`); treat `reported` items as leads. Forecasts carry a probability and
  a date and are scored publicly when they resolve.

## What the grades mean

- `confirmed`: established by the sources we read.
- `likely`: well supported but not fully established (for example, one strong source).
- `contested`: credible sources disagree.
- `unconfirmed` / `speculative`: reported but not established; treat as a lead.
- `opinion`: a stated view, attributed.

Grades are Ohmega's assessment as of the date shown, not a guarantee. When citing, give the article
URL and the claim id.

## Not verified by us

- [Headline radar](https://www.ohmega.monster/radar): daily headlines as other outlets reported them.
  These are leads, not verified claims. Do not treat them as Ohmega's findings.

## Rights

Our claims, summaries and grades may be quoted with a link. Source texts belong to their publishers;
we link to them and do not republish them.
